title: Food security depends on route quality, material adequacy, and layered buffers that are not interchangeable
source_unit: Deliberately non-pooled comparison of USDA/FNA SNAP route metrics, Urban WBNS food-security and charitable-food respondents, and SIPP person-month transitions
geography: United States; source-specific state, person-month, and respondent universes retained

observations.period: FY2025; USDA/FNA state SNAP route-performance context

denominator.unit: states and DC common to participation, application timeliness, and recertification timeliness

participation_vs_application_timeliness.unit: unweighted Pearson correlation across state/DC aggregates

participation_vs_recertification_timelin.unit: unweighted Pearson correlation across state/DC aggregates

observations.method: Cross-source extraction of USDA/FNA state participation, application-timeliness, and recertification-timeliness measures; state aggregates retain distinct population and quality-control denominators.
observations.uncertainty: Ecological state aggregates without case-mix adjustment, household effort, notice comprehension, benefit amount, gap days, or remedy. Correlations are descriptive and unweighted.
observations.counterinterpretation: Near-zero aggregate correlation does not mean route performance is irrelevant; it means participation cannot substitute for route quality or household security.

observations.period: December 2019-December 2025; Urban WBNS food-insecurity trend and 2025 subgroup context

denominator.unit: published WBNS working-age adults ages 18-64; exact annual analytic denominators not disclosed

observations.method: Urban Institute weighted WBNS six-item USDA short-form estimates; annual trend and subgroup estimates retain the source's age, income, household, race/ethnicity, and disability universes.
observations.uncertainty: Exact denominators and full variance tables are not disclosed in the brief; 2025 methodology changed and the trend is not a panel. Food insecurity does not identify SNAP receipt, benefit adequacy, route failure, or causation.
observations.subgroup: Working-age adults, families with children, income-to-poverty bands, and adults with disabilities.
observations.counterinterpretation: Annual movement can reflect prices, labor markets, household composition, pandemic supports, survey composition, and program access; subgroup differences do not identify one cause.

observations.period: December 2025; Urban WBNS charitable-food participation, access, and unmet need

denominator.unit: source-specific adult, food-insecure, charitable-food participant, and unmet-need universes; exact analytic denominators not disclosed

food_insecure_charitable_food.unit: percent of adults in food-insecure households

food_insecure_unmet_charitable_food.unit: percent of adults in food-insecure households

unmet_need_closed_when_available.unit: percent of adults with unmet need; multiple-response reason

unmet_need_did_not_know_where.unit: percent of adults with unmet need; multiple-response reason

unmet_need_not_comfortable.unit: percent of adults with unmet need; multiple-response reason

observations.method: Published weighted WBNS cross-sectional estimates of charitable-food receipt, access difficulty, and unmet need; multiple-response barriers remain separate.
observations.uncertainty: Exact denominators and full design-based variance are not disclosed in the brief. Participation is not adequacy, and the layer does not observe provider capacity, SNAP amount, same-episode timing, or later security.
observations.subgroup: Adults, working-age adults, food-insecure adults, charitable-food participants, and adults with unmet charitable-food need.
observations.counterinterpretation: Charitable-food receipt can indicate successful supplemental access or severe shortfall; nonreceipt can indicate no need or an unserved need. Hours, awareness, transport, safety, variety, and treatment can overlap.

observations.period: 2024; Census SIPP adjacent SNAP transitions and following hardship

denominator.unit: valid adjacent person-month transition pairs matched to Fay-BRR replicates; transition cells retain separate valid-pair universes

rent_hardship_no_to_yes.unit: percent; following-month hardship among 437 entry pairs

rent_hardship_yes_to_no.unit: percent; following-month hardship among 387 exit pairs

rent_hardship_yes_to_yes.unit: percent; following-month hardship among 33,041 stable receipt pairs

utility_hardship_no_to_yes.unit: percent; following-month hardship among 437 entry pairs

utility_hardship_yes_to_no.unit: percent; following-month hardship among 387 exit pairs

utility_hardship_yes_to_yes.unit: percent; following-month hardship among 33,041 stable receipt pairs

observations.method: SIPP person-month transition comparison using WPFINWGT and 240 Fay-BRR replicate weights; following-month hardship fields retain their own universes and timing boundaries.
observations.uncertainty: Descriptive transitions, not program effects; entry and exit cells are rare and the record does not observe notice, effort, benefit amount, gap days, appeal, food security, trust, or political action for the same episode.
observations.subgroup: Valid adjacent person-month SNAP transition pairs, split into entry, exit, and stable receipt states.
observations.counterinterpretation: Exit can reflect higher income, noncollection, renewal failure, family change, or another shock; continued receipt can coexist with hardship. Neither transition is a security score.

related_sources.claim: Prior route triangulation supplies USDA, WBNS, NBER, SIPP, and charitable-food architecture.
WBNS supplies the updated 2019-2025 food-insecurity trend and subgroup endpoints.
WBNS supplies charitable-food access, treatment, and unmet-need endpoints.
NBER and administrative studies supply route-to-participation mechanisms.

boundary: This is a non-pooled food-security and safety-net route/buffer bridge. It shows that formal route quality, food insecurity, charitable-food reach, unmet need, and following hardship are distinct stages. It does not establish benefit adequacy, causal route failure, provider capacity, same-episode food outcomes, trust, political action, or recovery. A linked or matched episode design remains required.
